region: Upper Rio Negro & upper Orinoco — Brazil, Colombia & Venezuela
description: The smallest Paracheirodon, living in very soft, acidic blackwater pools and flooded forest. Its blue-green stripe runs right into the tail base, while red is confined to a narrow band on the lower rear flank.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: upper Amazon basin — Peru, Colombia & Brazil)
description: A captive-bred neon strain with elongated, trailing dorsal, anal and tail fins; stripe and red belly are as in the wild form. The long fins make it slower and a target for fin-nipping tankmates.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: upper Amazon basin — Peru, Colombia & Brazil)
description: A farmed neon strain carrying extra reflective guanine over the head and nape, giving it a sparkling silvery crown. The blue line is shortened to the rear half of the body, above the usual red.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: upper Amazon basin — Peru, Colombia & Brazil)
description: A captive strain with most dark pigment missing, so the body looks pale gold while the eyes stay dark. The iridescent line and red rear survive but appear softer than in wild-type neons.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: upper Amazon basin — Peru, Colombia & Brazil)
description: A melanin-free farmed neon with pink eyes and a creamy body. Albinism removes only the black pigment, so a pale iridescent line and the red rear patch are still visible.

region: Guaporé, Paraguay & central Amazon basins — Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay & Argentina
description: A hardy, deep-red tetra of slow, heavily vegetated waters, marked by a black comma-shaped shoulder spot. Kept in small numbers it squabbles and nips the fins of slow, long-finned tankmates.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: Guaporé & Paraguay basins, South America)
description: A line-bred serpae with long, trailing dorsal, anal and tail fins. It keeps the wild form's red body and black shoulder comma — and much of its nippy temperament.

region: Upper Paraguay & Guaporé basins — Mato Grosso, Brazil & Bolivia
description: A smoky-gray tetra with a large black shoulder blotch ringed in silver. Males stage harmless sparring displays with fully spread jet-black fins, while females show red ventral and adipose fins.

region: Upper Orinoco & Meta river basins — Colombia & Venezuela
description: A blood-red phantom tetra from cool, soft, tannin-stained tributaries of the Orinoco. It prefers cooler water than most tetras, and males flare their red-and-black dorsal fins at one another in brief displays.

region: Guiana Shield — Suriname & French Guiana
description: A tiny golden relative of the black and red phantom tetras, found in shaded forest creeks of the Guianas. A dark shoulder mark and white-tipped ventral fins set off its translucent yellow body.

region: Upper Amazon basin — Peru, Colombia & Brazil
description: A tall, rosy-silver tetra of quiet forest streams, named for the bright red spot over its heart. Mature males grow a long, sickle-shaped black-and-white dorsal fin and an extended anal fin.

region: Middle Rio Negro, Amazonas, Brazil
description: A Rio Negro relative of the bleeding heart, named for the fiery red that runs along its back above a pale violet flank. Exported wild-caught, it does best in very soft, acidic, tannin-stained water.

region: Middle Rio Negro, Amazonas, Brazil
description: A smaller, Rio Negro cousin of the bleeding heart tetra with a darker, maroon shoulder spot and a lilac sheen. It was named after the aquarium-fish importer Ross Socolof.

region: Guyana, Suriname & French Guiana — slow coastal rivers
description: A delicate pink tetra of slow, plant-choked Guianan streams with a black dorsal flag tipped in white, taller in males. It scatters adhesive eggs among fine-leaved plants at dawn.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: Guyana, Suriname & French Guiana)
description: A popular line-bred rosy tetra whose dorsal, anal and tail fins trail far beyond the normal outline. The black-and-white dorsal flag becomes a tall, flowing banner in males.

region: Lower & middle Amazon basin, Brazil
description: Very like the rosy tetra but lacking a shoulder spot; mature males carry a tall, white-tipped black dorsal fin. It lives among submerged vegetation and roots along the lower Amazon and its tributaries.

region: Central & upper Amazon basin — Brazil & Peru
description: A member of the rosy-tetra group from the central Amazon, with an amber-red body, a dark vertical shoulder mark and a white-tipped black dorsal fin. It is often confused with the serpae and rosy tetras.

region: Coastal streams around Rio de Janeiro, south-eastern Brazil
description: Also called the Von Rio tetra, it comes from coastal streams around Rio de Janeiro, much of which has been lost to urban growth, so aquarium stocks are almost all captive-bred. Two black bars mark the shoulder and the rear body glows red.

region: Upper Tocantins basin — Goiás, Brazil
description: A small, copper-red tetra from the upper Tocantins basin that closely resembles the flame tetra. It is told apart by the white tips on its dorsal, anal and pelvic fins.

region: Upper Paraguay basin (Rio Taquari) — Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil
description: From streams feeding the Pantanal, it carries a brilliant greenish-white line above a broad velvet-black band, with a red crescent over the eye. Hardy, peaceful and widely captive-bred.

region: Rio Araguaia basin — Mato Grosso & Tocantins, Brazil
description: A tiny orange tetra named after Amanda Bleher, mother of the explorer Heiko Bleher. It lives among dense vegetation in slow tributaries and floodplain lakes of the Araguaia, feeding on minute invertebrates and zooplankton.

region: Rio Tapajós basin, Pará, Brazil
description: A translucent lemon-yellow tetra whose anal fin carries a bright yellow leading edge bordered in black, beneath an eye ringed red above. Males hold small display stations within the shoal and spread their fins at rivals.

region: Coastal rivers of south-eastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro to Rio Grande do Sul)
description: A subtropical tetra of clear coastal streams in south-eastern Brazil, named for the two dark vertical bars behind its gill cover. Mature males develop reddish anal and pelvic fins, while females stay yellow.

region: Río Acandí drainage, Caribbean slope of north-western Colombia
description: Known from a small coastal drainage near the Panama border, this robust tetra pairs an iridescent blue upper body with bright red fins. Hardy and boisterous, it can nip the fins of slow tankmates.

region: Lower Amazon & Tocantins basins, Pará, Brazil
description: Named for its three-coloured lateral "flag": a red band over a gold line over a black stripe that runs back to the tail. Also sold as the false Ulrey's tetra, after a very similar species that is rarely exported.

region: Upper & middle Amazon basin — Brazil (Rio Madeira), Bolivia & Peru
description: A slim tetra whose broad black lateral band runs from behind the gill cover into the middle of the tail, framed by a blood-red caudal fin and a red crescent over the eye. It shoals in slow, shaded tributaries and flooded forest.

region: Upper Amazon — Loreto, Peru & Amazonas, Colombia
description: A small Peruvian tetra with a broad black lateral band topped by a shining gold line and red-tinged fins. It lives in slow, shaded forest streams with soft, acidic water.

region: Lower Amazon basin & coastal rivers of Pará, Brazil
description: A hardy, silvery tetra with a thin black line along the rear flank that ends in a dark diamond on the tail base. It tolerates a wide range of water conditions and spawns readily among fine-leaved plants.

region: Upper Rio Tapajós basin (Rio Juruena), Mato Grosso, Brazil
description: A slender tetra from clear tributaries of the upper Tapajós, marked by a black band along the rear half of the body under a pale gold line and a red crescent over the eye.

region: Coastal drainages of Amapá, northern Brazil
description: Named for the large, bean-shaped black blotch behind its gill cover, this small tetra has a brassy, translucent body and a second dark mark on the tail base. It comes from soft, tannin-stained coastal streams.

region: Essequibo basin, Guyana & rivers of Suriname
description: A modest golden tetra from the Guiana Shield with a dark spot on the tail base and red-orange tints in the tail and anal fins. It shoals in shaded, slow-moving forest streams.

region: Essequibo River basin, Guyana
description: From the Essequibo basin of Guyana, its translucent body carries a single glowing orange-red stripe from the snout through the eye to the tail. Almost all aquarium stock is farm-bred.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: Essequibo basin, Guyana)
description: A farmed albino strain of the glowlight tetra with pink-red eyes and a creamy, see-through body. Without black pigment the orange stripe and white fin tips stand out even more.

region: Amazon basin & coastal rivers of the Guianas — Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Suriname & French Guiana
description: Also called the beacon tetra: a red-gold crescent over the eye and a shining gold spot on the upper tail base catch the light above a black tail-base spot. It is a hardy, active shoaler of slow, vegetated waters.

region: Upper Amazon basin, Peru
description: A deep-bodied tetra from the Peruvian Amazon with a coppery-pink sheen and a black wedge along the rear flank capped by a shining gold line. The upper half of the eye is bright red.

region: Guianas & lower Amazon — Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana & Brazil
description: Wild fish often wear a brassy gold sheen, thought to be a guanine reaction of the skin to trematode parasites; captive-bred fish are usually plainer silver. A black blotch marks the tail base.

region: Central & upper Amazon — Brazil, Peru & Colombia
description: Named after Lake Hyanuary near Manaus, it has a translucent, greenish body with an iridescent green-gold line along the upper flank ending above a black spot on the tail base. It is also sold as the Costello tetra.

region: Amazon & Orinoco basins — Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela & Guyana
description: A silvery tetra marked by bright red at the base of both tail lobes and a red crescent over the eye. It shoals in clear to tea-stained tributaries of the Rio Negro and upper Orinoco.

region: Trinidad, the Guianas and the Orinoco & Amazon basins
description: A hardy, silvery-olive tetra named for the black-and-white front rays of its anal fin, which look like a small feather. It ranges from Trinidad across the Guianas into the Amazon.

region: Rio São Francisco basin, Brazil
description: A copper-gold tetra whose dorsal, anal, tail and pelvic fins are tipped bright white; unlike most tetras it lacks an adipose fin. Males are deep copper, females paler yellow-silver.

region: Lower Amazon basin, Pará, Brazil
description: Formerly Hemigrammus rhodostoma, it schools tightly with its black-and-white striped tails flicking in unison. The red face pales quickly under stress or in poor water, making it a living water-quality indicator.

region: Rio Negro & Rio Meta basins — Brazil & Colombia
description: The rummy-nose most often sold today; its blood-red face extends behind the gill cover onto the front of the body. It schools tightly in soft, acidic blackwater streams.

region: Upper Amazon basin, Peru
description: The type species of Petitella, from the Peruvian Amazon. Its red is paler and confined mostly to the snout, and a thin black line runs forward from the striped tail along the rear half of the body.

region: Paraná, Paraguay & São Francisco basins and western Amazon — Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia & Peru
description: A hardy, robust tetra with large dark-edged scales, a vivid red crescent above the eye and a broad black band across the tail base behind a pale gold one. Active and boisterous, it may nip slow, long-finned fish.

region: Lake Valencia basin & nearby rivers, northern Venezuela
description: From the Lake Valencia basin of Venezuela; its large scales sparkle like glitter, and mature males grow long, flowing, violet-tinged dorsal and anal fins. The full colours take a year or more to develop.

region: Guianas & Amazon basin — Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana, Brazil & Peru
description: Larger and stockier than the red-eye tetra it resembles, with net-like dark-edged scales, a red crescent over the eye and a black tail-base band behind a cream-yellow saddle. It is a hardy, active shoaler that may nip fins.

region: Amazon, Orinoco & Paraguay basins
description: A slender, silvery tetra immediately recognised by the black stripe running along the middle of each tail lobe. It is an active, open-water shoaler of rivers and floodplain lakes.

region: Paraná basin — Argentina, Paraguay & southern Brazil
description: A subtropical tetra with a silvery, blue-green-sheened body and blood-red tail base, anal and pelvic fins. A fast swimmer of the upper water, it scatters its eggs near the surface over plants.

region: Paraguay & lower Paraná basins — Paraguay, Brazil & Argentina
description: A small relative of the bloodfin with an iridescent green-blue upper body, a red lower rear flank and red, white-tipped fins. It shoals actively in quiet, vegetated backwaters.

region: Amazon & Paraná basins — Brazil, Peru, Bolivia & Paraguay
description: A glass-clear, surface-loving characin with a blood-red tail base. Males develop a long white filament at the front of the anal fin, displayed during courtship.

region: Amazon & Orinoco basins and coastal rivers of the Guianas
description: Its see-through body reveals the swim bladder and spine, and its dorsal, anal and pelvic fins carry bold yellow, black and white bands. Unusually for a tetra it also lives in slightly brackish coastal waters.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: Amazon, Orinoco & Guiana coastal rivers)
description: A farmed albino (golden) strain of the X-ray tetra with pink-red eyes. Lacking black pigment, its fins show only yellow and white on a pale gold, see-through body.

region: Upper Amazon & Araguaia basins — Peru & Brazil
description: A black stripe runs from the gill cover along the body and bends down into the lower tail lobe like a hockey stick. It rests at a head-up angle and is a notorious jumper.

region: Amazon basin, Brazil
description: Very like the common penguin tetra, but its black band begins only around the dorsal fin rather than at the gill cover before sweeping down into the lower tail lobe. It too hangs at a head-up angle and jumps readily.

region: Rio Aripuanã & upper Rio Madeira basin — Mato Grosso & Amazonas, Brazil
description: Also sold as the blue emperor, it is named after INPA, the Brazilian Amazon research institute. Males are violet-blue above a dark lateral band, while females are yellowish-brown with a reddish adipose fin.

region: Río San Juan & Río Atrato basins, Pacific slope of western Colombia
description: A velvet-black lateral band, violet-blue sheen and black-edged yellow fins mark this Colombian tetra; mature males grow a three-pointed tail with an extended central ray. Like its congener it lacks an adipose fin, and males defend small territories among plants.

region: Captive-bred (dark form of a western Colombian species)
description: A dark trade form of the emperor tetra in which the black lateral band spreads over most of the body, leaving a blue-violet sheen above and pale fin edges. It shares the territorial habits and trident tail of the normal form.

region: Río San Juan basin, western Colombia
description: A sister species of the emperor tetra whose males have bright red eyes and a rainbow sheen of red, green and blue over a dark lateral band; females have greenish eyes. Like the emperor it lacks an adipose fin.

region: Upper Río Meta basin, Colombia
description: A tiny, translucent tetra from the Meta basin that turns deep ruby red all over in good condition, males most intensely. It lives among plants and leaf litter in soft, acidic water.

region: Upper Amazon (Marañón basin) — Peru & Colombia
description: A slim, steel-blue tetra whose iridescent sheen shifts from turquoise to violet as it turns. It is a lively shoaler of shallow upper-Amazon streams and can nip slow tankmates.

region: Upper Rio Negro — Rio Uaupés (Vaupés) tributaries, Amazonas, Brazil
description: One of the smallest characins, described in 1997 from blackwater streams of the upper Rio Negro. Its translucent amber body carries a dark band along the flank with a fine iridescent line above it.

region: Paraguay & Guaporé basins — Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay & Argentina
description: Also called the black skirt tetra: two black bars cross the front half of its deep body, and the rear and the skirt-like anal fin are jet black, fading to smoky gray in older fish. Hardy and active, it can nip long-finned tankmates.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: Paraguay & Guaporé basins)
description: A line-bred black widow with greatly elongated, veil-like dorsal, anal and tail fins. It keeps the bars and black skirt of the wild form, but the long fins slow it and draw nips from other fish.

region: Captive-bred (wild form: Paraguay & Guaporé basins)
description: A pale farm strain of the black widow tetra with a milky, translucent body and white fins; the dark shoulder bars are faint or missing. Behaviour, including fin-nipping, is that of the wild form.

region: Captive-bred (genetically modified line of the black widow tetra)
description: A trademarked, genetically modified black widow tetra whose inherited fluorescent protein colours it vivid red and makes it glow under blue (actinic) light. Behaviour is that of the ordinary black widow, including a tendency to nip fins.

region: Captive-bred (genetically modified line of the black widow tetra)
description: A GloFish line of the black widow tetra carrying a gene for a green fluorescent protein, so it shines neon green under blue light. The colour is inherited, not dyed, and is passed on to its offspring.

region: Captive-bred (genetically modified line of the black widow tetra)
description: A genetically modified black widow tetra that is fluorescent orange from snout to fin tips; the colour is inherited rather than injected or dyed. The faint shoulder bars of the wild form still show through.

region: Captive-bred (genetically modified line of the black widow tetra)
description: A GloFish black widow tetra with an inherited blue fluorescent protein that shows best under actinic lighting. In white light it looks a deep, slightly violet blue.

region: Captive-bred (genetically modified line of the black widow tetra)
description: A GloFish line of the black widow tetra coloured deep violet-purple by an inherited fluorescent protein. It glows most strongly under blue light and behaves exactly like the wild species.

region: Captive-bred (genetically modified line of the black widow tetra)
description: A GloFish black widow tetra with a bright fluorescent-pink body and fins. The colour comes from an inherited fluorescent protein and is passed on to its offspring.

region: Lower Rio Grande & Pecos drainages (Texas & New Mexico) south through eastern Mexico
description: The northernmost native characin, ranging from Texas into eastern Mexico; the river form is a silvery, fully sighted fish with a dark stripe toward the tail and yellow-red tinted fins. Several cave populations of the same species have evolved into the eyeless blind cave tetra.

region: Limestone caves of the Sierra de El Abra region — San Luis Potosí & Tamaulipas, Mexico
description: Cave populations of the Mexican tetra have lost their eyes and pigment: eyes begin to form in the embryo, then degenerate under the skin. They find food with an enlarged lateral line and extra taste buds, and sleep far less than river fish.

region: Northern & eastern South America — Guianas, Venezuela & Brazil
description: A robust, silvery characin with a horizontally oval black shoulder spot and a second black spot at the tail base that continues into the middle tail rays. An opportunistic omnivore of rivers and lakes, it eats insects, seeds and fallen fruit.

region: Paraná–La Plata basin — Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay & southern Brazil
description: A hardy subtropical tetra long sold as Hemigrammus caudovittatus or Hyphessobrycon anisitsi, with a black cross-shaped mark on the tail base and red-tinged fins. It is a notorious eater of soft aquarium plants.

region: Coastal rivers of northern South America — Venezuela to the Guianas
description: A deep, compressed, glittering silver tetra with a dark spot on the tail base. Hardy and long-lived, it eats soft plants and may nip fins.

region: Trinidad, northern Venezuela & Colombia
description: Males carry a long, paddle-like extension of the gill cover that they flick in front of females during courtship. Fertilisation is internal: females store sperm and later lay fertilised eggs on their own.

region: Southern Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay & north-eastern Argentina
description: A subtropical characin whose males grow huge, wing-like dorsal and anal fins that they spread in courtship displays. As in the swordtail characin, fertilisation is internal and females can store sperm.

region: Atlantic Forest coastal streams of south-eastern Brazil
description: A slender, surface-dwelling characin of cool, shaded Atlantic Forest streams; males shimmer blue-green above a dark lateral band. Fertilisation is internal, and males court females with elaborate fin displays.
